title: What If Every Earthworm Vanished Overnight?

scenes.text: What if every earthworm vanished overnight? Your dinner would feel it first.
Earthworms pull dead leaves underground, releasing nutrients, mainly nitrogen, that plants need.
Their tunnels let rainwater soak in instead of running off, and help soil resist erosion.
A 2023 study estimated they add about six and a half percent of the world's grain, and two point three percent of its legumes.
That's roughly one hundred forty million tons of food every year. In sub-Saharan Africa, up to ten percent of grain.
And the authors think the real number is bigger. We just haven't counted worms across much of the tropics.
